headline: High: Roo Code’s filesystem/MCP/browser access can interact dangerously with a prompt-leak target, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP; its shared state is via filesystem, so attacker-controlled content from system_prompts_leaks could be surfaced into prompts or tool flows. system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage, making the interaction plausible even though direct bridging is undocumented.
conditions: IF agent_b content is copied into a Roo Code workspace file or MCP-fed context, then prompt injection is possible.
IF Roo Code parses untrusted text from agent_b as instructions, then tool hijacking risk materializes.
mitigations: Disable MCP servers for the session.
Keep agent_b content out of shared workspace files.
Use a read-only review mode for untrusted text.
Require manual approval for every tool action.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code and browser screenshots and can egress broadly, while system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak repository with no declared data handling. The pair can leak sensitive workspace material if agent_b content is mixed into Roo Code’s context or outputs, but the evidence does not show a default shared workspace with sensitive data.
conditions: IF sensitive source code is present in the Roo Code workspace and copied into agent_b-related prompts, then leakage occurs.
IF Roo Code sends browser screenshots or workspace text to a third-party model API, then data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before use.
Turn off browser capture for sensitive sessions.
Use a local-only model endpoint.
Separate prompt-leak review files from production code.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound model requests.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, git modification, and broad network egress in a per-workspace model with shared state via filesystem. system_prompts_leaks is source-available and may be used as a mutable artifact or reference set; if both touch the same workspace, write conflicts and git-state races are likely. Uncertainty about agent_b’s mutability pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace directory, then file clobbering can occur.
IF both agents modify the same git branch without locking, then commit races occur.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces.
Freeze git writes during parallel runs.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Make agent_b outputs read-only artifacts.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on browser and filesystem outputs, so if it consumes agent_b material as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or tool actions. system_prompts_leaks is not documented as a verifier, so the pair lacks a built-in verification step; however, the downstream blast radius is not shown to be irreversible by default.
conditions: IF agent_b output is fed into Roo Code without verification, then Roo Code may act on false premises.
IF Roo Code uses agent_b-derived text as instructions, then erroneous tool actions can cascade.
mitigations: Require a human review step before execution.
Treat agent_b output as untrusted input.
Cross-check claims against primary sources.
Limit Roo Code to read-only mode for review tasks.
requires-engineering: add automated fact verification.

E_compliance.rationale: Roo Code handles model provider API keys and can send data to configured APIs, while system_prompts_leaks is a source-available repository with no stated compliance controls. The main issue is a potential policy mismatch if regulated data is placed into Roo Code and then exposed through its configured provider; the pair itself does not prove a residency or certification violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Roo Code and sent to a non-compliant provider, then a compliance breach occurs.
IF the operator relies on agent_b as a compliant storage or processing system, then policy gaps appear.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the workspace.
Use a provider with the required compliance posture.
Review retention settings before use.
Document data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: implement compliance-aware routing.
